newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: New Namibian fishing company formed.
newsitem.headline: New Namibian fishing company formed.

text.p: Uneconomic quota allocations and poor catch rates off the Namibian coastline have resulted in the establishment of a new joint venture fishing company to maximise resources.

Irvin & Johnson Ltd and Naras Investment (Pty) Ltd subsidiary Kuiseb Fish Products Ltd and the Ohlthaver and List Group's Consortium Fisheries said they had joined forces to overcome the difficulties which had affected the Namibian offshore fishing industry in recent years.
I&J will have the marketing, sales and distribution rights to the company's products in southern African and certain other countries.

Kuiseb chairman Festus Naholo said in a statement that the new company, to be called Hangana Seafood (Pty) Ltd, had the potential to play an increasingly important role in the Namibian fishing industry.
Consortium Fisheries will own 60 percent of the new company and Kuiseb the remaining 40 percent.
I&J reported a loss of more than 20 million rand in its Namibian fishing business in the year ended June 1996.
